mood.p: Zaterdag 5 september brengt een afwisseling van stapelwolken en zon, met in de noordelijke helft van het land misschien een enkele bui. Door een westenwind is het iets frisser dan vrijdag, met maxima tussen 20 en 22 graden, terwijl de code geel voor harde windstoten aan de kust is opgeheven. Zondag en maandag draait de wind naar het zuiden en wordt het zomers warm, met 27 tot 28 graden en in het zuiden mogelijk zelfs 30. De stemming in het land is dit weekend gemengd: de schok van het geweld in Overasselt werkt nog na, nu 32 verdachten vastzitten en minister Van Weel benadrukt dat Nederland geen narcostaat is. In Den Haag maakt het kabinet-Jetten zich op voor Prinsjesdag op 15 september, terwijl een peiling van Ipsos I&O laat zien dat nog maar 18 procent van de kiezers tevreden is. Havenwerkers legden vrijdag het werk neer en woensdag dreigt een landelijke ov-staking, dus veel Nederlanders plannen hun week met een schuin oog op de nieuwsapp. Het nazomerweer nodigt intussen uit tot een laatste strandbezoek of terrasje.

global.h3: Trump calls Iran war 'small potatoes' as US and Iran trade Hormuz strikes
global.summary: Trump called the Iran war 'small potatoes' on 4 September, a day after Vance stopped short of calling it a war. Eighteen US troops have died as Hormuz strikes continue.
body: Speaking on Friday 4 September, President Trump described the Iran conflict as a military operation rather than a war, calling it 'small potatoes' and comparing it favourably with Vietnam and Afghanistan. Vice President Vance had said a day earlier that major combat operations lasted only six weeks.

The war began on 28 February 2026 with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran. CNN reports 18 US service members have died and hundreds are injured at a cost of more than 37.5 billion dollars, as US strikes resumed near the Strait of Hormuz this week and Iran hit bases in Kuwait and the UAE in retaliation.

global.h3: US probes deadly wedding strike in Iran as analysis points to American missile
global.summary: Washington is investigating a 1 September strike on an Iran wedding that killed at least four. Experts told Reuters the damage matched a direct US missile hit.
body: A missile hit a wedding in Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, on the night of 1 September. Iran's Red Crescent said four people died, including a four year old boy and a 16 year old, and 67 were injured, though Iranian media later put the toll at five.

Weapons experts reviewing footage for Reuters and the New York Times said on 3 September the blast likely came from a direct US hit, with fragments resembling a SLAM-ER missile. Vance confirmed the US is investigating, and the Red Crescent asked the ICC to act.

global.h3: Iran hits US bases in Kuwait and UAE in retaliation for bombardments
global.summary: Iran said it struck US bases in Kuwait and the UAE on 3 September, calling it retaliation for the Kuhestak strike. Israel warned economic strain could push Iran further.
body: Iran said on 3 September it struck bases used by US forces in Kuwait and the UAE, calling it retaliation for bombardments including the Kuhestak wedding strike. Iranian media also reported six navy personnel killed near the Strait of Hormuz.

The exchanges mark the worst escalation since June's truce framework, with Iran also claiming strikes on US-linked sites in Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq. Israel's defence minister said Iran's leadership fears economic collapse, which could push Tehran toward reckless action.

global.h3: Putin sees chance of Ukraine deal as Belgorod strike kills four
global.summary: Putin said on 3 September a Ukraine deal is possible, with the US and China ready to back a settlement. A Ukrainian strike on Belgorod killed four the same day.
body: Vladimir Putin told reporters on 3 September he saw a chance of an agreement to end the war in Ukraine, saying the United States and China were prepared to support a settlement. He said a Ukrainian warning to civil aviation had complicated matters, Reuters reported.

Fighting continued regardless. Regional officials said a Ukrainian strike on Belgorod killed four people including two medical workers, while Russia Matters found Russian forces gained about 40 square miles of Ukrainian territory in the four weeks to 1 September.

global.h3: Trump wants Europe to repay US for Ukraine weapons
global.summary: Trump said on 3 September he will ask Europe to repay the US for Ukraine weapons and hinted at pausing arms sales as US stockpiles run low after the Iran war.
body: In a social media post on 3 September, Donald Trump said he would ask European nations to repay the United States for weapons and ammunition sent to Ukraine, and signalled a possible halt to arms sales to allies. Reuters said the administration has not explained how repayment would work.

The demand follows Trump's complaints that six months of operations against Iran have depleted US munitions stocks. It lands as the EU struggles with its own Russia policy after Slovakia blocked a 12 month extension of the bloc's sanctions this week.

global.h3: Zelensky orders probe into shootout between Ukrainian security agencies
global.summary: Zelensky said on 3 September an investigation is under way after a dispute between two Ukrainian security agencies turned into a shootout.
body: Volodymyr Zelensky said on 3 September that investigators are trying to establish how a dispute between two Ukrainian security agencies escalated into gunfire. The incident has embarrassed Kyiv as it tries to show unity to Western backers.

Reuters reported the row centres on the nine day disappearance of a Russian nationalist activist fighting for Ukraine, who says the SBU detained him and pressured him into a confession he later withdrew. Zelensky did not name the second agency, and officials promise findings once the inquiry ends.

global.h3: Israel clears Hezbollah tunnels on Ali al-Taher ridge, frees five Lebanese
global.summary: Israel said on 3 September it cleared Hezbollah fighters from tunnels on Lebanon's Ali al-Taher ridge and will destroy the complex, while freeing five Lebanese detainees.
body: The Israel Defense Forces said on 3 September that troops cleared Hezbollah militants from tunnels inside the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon and intend to neutralise the complex. The ridge has been repeatedly struck since Lebanon was drawn into the wider war in March.

Separately, Netanyahu's office said Israel would free five Lebanese citizens found to have no ties to armed groups. Reuters says 35 Lebanese detainees remain in Israeli custody, including about 20 civilians, as indirect talks continue.

global.h3: German police probe fresh sabotage attempts on power grid
global.summary: German police responded on 4 September to two suspected attacks on the power grid, including one in Dormagen with a claim letter, Bild reported.
body: German police reacted on 4 September to two fresh suspected attempts to sabotage the electricity grid, Bild reported. A letter claiming responsibility was received for one attempt in Dormagen, near Cologne, though its authenticity is still being checked.

The incidents follow a string of attacks on energy and defence sites this year, including a suspected arson attack in Munich on Thursday outside a defence technology firm that led to two arrests. Authorities have repeatedly warned about hybrid threats to critical infrastructure.

global.h3: Syria begins destroying Assad-era chemical weapons remnants
global.summary: A Syrian envoy and a UN representative confirmed on 3 September that Damascus has begun destroying chemical weapons material recovered in May from the former regime.
body: Syria has begun destroying remnants of the chemical weapons programme built under Bashar al-Assad, a Syrian envoy and a UN representative confirmed on 3 September. The material was recovered in May after new authorities gained access to previously hidden sites.

The destruction is being carried out with international oversight, and Reuters says the process will take time given the volume and condition of the recovered stocks. Western governments have made verified disarmament a condition for further sanctions relief and reconstruction support.

global.h3: US rejects Israeli calls to remove Palestinians from Gaza
global.summary: The State Department told Al Jazeera on 4 September that Washington opposes any forced displacement from Gaza, after Israel's Katz said emigration was the only solution.
body: The US State Department said on 4 September it opposes forced displacement, expulsion or transfer of Gaza's population, citing Point 12 of Trump's peace plan. This followed Israeli Defence Minister Katz saying Israel was ready to move Palestinians out by sea, air or other means.

National Security Minister Ben-Gvir echoed the call a day later. The October 2025 ceasefire remains formally in place, but Israeli strikes killed at least three people in Gaza on Thursday, and Arab governments have rejected any relocation scheme.

global.h3: Slovakia blocks 12-month extension of EU sanctions on Russia
global.summary: Slovakia was the lone holdout on 2 September as EU governments tried to extend the bloc's individual sanctions on Russia to a full year, diplomats told Politico.
body: The Slovak government rejected a proposal on 2 September to extend the EU's individual sanctions package on Russia to 12 months instead of the usual six, three diplomats told Politico. Slovakia was the only member state to object.

The longer renewal was meant to shield sanctions from repeated veto threats and any shift in US policy, but without unanimity listings will keep coming up for renewal every six months. Robert Fico's government has repeatedly used sanctions rounds to extract energy concessions.

global.h3: Milei threatens sanctions on oil firms drilling off the Falklands
global.summary: Milei said on 3 September Argentina will sanction oil firms drilling near the Falklands. London replied that islanders have the right to their own resources.
body: Javier Milei said on 3 September that Argentina would sanction oil companies drilling in waters around the Falkland Islands, which Buenos Aires calls the Malvinas and claims as its own. He called the exploration plans of two firms a pressing threat and promised a tougher defence posture.

Downing Street responded on 4 September that the Falkland Islanders' right of self-determination extends to their natural resources, the BBC reported. Analysts told Reuters the move plays to domestic nationalism ahead of a difficult economic period for Argentina.

global.h3: Philippine court orders arrest of Vice President Sara Duterte
global.summary: A Quezon City court issued a warrant on 4 September for Vice President Sara Duterte over her 2025 remark about arranging a hitman to kill President Marcos.
body: The Quezon City court issued an arrest warrant on 4 September for VP Sara Duterte on three counts of grave threats, lawyer Paul Lawrence Lim said, with bail set at 120,000 pesos per count. The case stems from a November 2025 press conference where Duterte said she told an assassin to kill President Marcos and First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos if she were killed.
She later said the comment was not literal. Lim said Duterte disputes the court's jurisdiction but will not evade the law, deepening the feud between the Marcos and Duterte families.

global.h3: Pacific leaders voice concern over China missile test, Nauru dissents
global.summary: Pacific Island leaders issued a statement on 3 September on China's July missile test over the region, with Nauru formally dissenting.
body: Leaders at the Pacific Islands Forum summit adopted a statement on 3 September expressing concern about China's intercontinental ballistic missile test in July, which passed over several island nations without adequate notice. Nauru, one of Beijing's closest regional partners, formally dissented.

China's Foreign Ministry said the country remains committed to peaceful development and called the test routine. Reuters said the disagreement shows how Beijing, Washington and Canberra competition is straining the forum's tradition of consensus.

global.h3: US sanctions Raul Castro's grandson and five Cuban companies
global.summary: The State Department sanctioned Raul Castro's grandson and five Cuban firms on 3 September, tightening pressure on Havana.
body: The US State Department announced sanctions on 3 September against five Cuban companies and Fidel Ernesto Castro, a grandson of former leader Raul Castro, designated as an adult family member of other sanctioned Castros. The targets include a state bank, two nickel mining firms and two energy companies, Reuters reported.

The measures freeze any US-linked assets and bar American firms from dealing with them. The move continues the Trump administration's hard line on Havana as Cuba faces severe power shortages and record emigration.

global.h3: Nepal flood toll passes 1,250 as thousands remain missing
global.summary: Nepal's flood death toll rose to 1,252 by 3 September, with more than 4,000 still missing. PM Balendra Shah says focus is shifting to rehabilitation.
body: Nepal's disaster authority said 1,252 bodies had been recovered as of 3 September from floods that hit Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading a week earlier, up from 1,114, with 4,216 still missing. More than 84,000 people are affected, while China reported 16 deaths and about 546 missing in Tibet.

More than 21,000 Nepali soldiers and police have deployed and the government released about 6.5 million dollars for reconstruction, with 48 bridges damaged. The US is tracking 75 unaccounted Americans, and three Dutch nationals remain missing.

global.h3: France counts 7,000 excess deaths from summer heatwaves
global.summary: French Health Minister Rist said on 4 September that about 7,000 excess deaths were recorded during this summer's heatwaves, a day after Belgium reported roughly 3,000.
body: France recorded about 7,000 excess deaths during this summer's heatwaves, Health Minister Stephanie Rist said on 4 September, one of the highest figures since the 2003 heatwave that killed some 15,000 people. Belgium announced on Thursday roughly 3,000 excess deaths from summer heat.

Both governments said the elderly and people with chronic illness accounted for most deaths. The figures add to evidence that repeated heat extremes are now a leading cause of weather-related mortality across Western Europe.

global.h3: Haiti urges UN to renew anti-gang force before December election
global.summary: Haiti's foreign minister asked the UN Security Council on 3 September to renew the anti-gang force's mandate ahead of the country's first election in a decade.
body: Foreign Minister Raina Forbin urged the UN Security Council on 3 September to renew the 12 month mandate of the international force backing Haiti's police against armed gangs, saying stronger support is needed for December's election. Gangs still control large parts of Port-au-Prince and key roads.

Reuters said council members broadly support renewal but differ on financing. The plea came as the US deported more than 100 people to Haiti on Thursday, the third consecutive weekly flight, despite warnings from rights groups.

global.h3: Saxony-Anhalt votes Sunday with AfD poised for first state victory
global.summary: Saxony-Anhalt votes on Sunday 6 September with the AfD polling above 40 percent, raising the prospect of its first state governorship since the war.
body: Saxony-Anhalt holds its state election on 6 September, with the AfD leading polls at around 41.7 percent, projected to win 39 seats ahead of the CDU on 21 and Die Linke on 11. A majority could let it govern alone despite the firewall policy under which other parties refuse to cooperate with it.

NPR said the party's rise has been fuelled by a strong TikTok presence among younger voters. Tactical voting drives are urging support for smaller parties to keep the AfD from power, and the result will be watched in Berlin and Brussels.

global.h3: Judge extends block on Trump order limiting mail-in voting
global.summary: A federal judge extended her block on Trump's mail voting restrictions on 4 September, a day after the Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to intervene.
body: A federal judge on 4 September extended her order stopping the US Postal Service from enforcing Trump's executive order limiting mail voting in November's midterms, the AP reported. The ruling keeps the status quo while litigation continues.

The Justice Department had filed an emergency request on Thursday asking the Supreme Court to lift the block, arguing it conflicts with the court's earlier decision to lift a separate injunction in June. Election officials say they need certainty soon because overseas and military ballots must go out in September.

global.h3: Pentagon still labels Anthropic a supply chain risk, contradicting Lutnick
global.summary: Pentagon official Emil Michael said on 3 September Anthropic remains on its risk list, contradicting Commerce Secretary Lutnick's claim a day earlier.
body: Emil Michael, the Pentagon's top technology official, said on 3 September Anthropic is still a supply chain risk, Axios reported, contradicting Lutnick's claim a day earlier that it was back in good standing. Politico reported Meta's Zuckerberg told Trump in an undisclosed call that a national AI regulator was a flawed idea.

The mixed messages reflect a wider administration struggle over regulating AI. Separately, the Los Angeles school district said it will heavily restrict student use of AI chatbots, including Google's Gemini, across all grades.

netherlands.h3: 32 held over Overasselt attack, Van Weel says Netherlands is no narco state
netherlands.summary: 32 suspects were remanded on 4 September over the Overasselt shooting that killed guard Berry Leenders. Van Weel vowed to catch fugitive Leijdekkers.
body: An examining magistrate ordered 32 suspects to remain in custody on 4 September over the armed raid on a home in Overasselt on 1 September, prosecutors confirmed. The group includes 16 French, 11 Dutch, two Algerian, one Libyan, one Ukrainian and one Belgian national, aged 18 to 32 apart from two French boys of 16 and 17.

All face charges including the murder of security guard Berry Leenders, 51, attempted murder of two wounded officers and weapons possession, in an attack targeting alleged trafficker Jan G Junior over a missing 1,900 kilogram cocaine shipment. Justice Minister David van Weel said the Netherlands is not a narco state and vowed to pursue fugitive Jos 'Bolle Jos' Leijdekkers.

netherlands.h3: Only 18 percent of voters satisfied with Jetten cabinet, Ipsos I&O finds
netherlands.summary: An Ipsos I&O poll published on 4 September found cabinet satisfaction at its lowest since February, with seven in ten voters dissatisfied and PRO the largest party.
body: An Ipsos I&O survey for WNL, published on 4 September, found just 18 percent approve of the cabinet's policies, down from 26 percent in July, with 70 percent dissatisfied. D66, CDA and VVD voters are cooling too, at 51, 43 and 32 percent satisfied.

Researchers link the slump to fraught budget talks, with voters mostly blaming the VVD, and only 9 percent trust the cabinet to solve problems. If elections were held now, PRO would be largest with 26 seats and D66 would fall to 20, in a survey of 2,100 people.

netherlands.h3: Jetten files police complaint over leaked budget documents
netherlands.summary: Jetten said on 4 September the cabinet will report the leak of confidential Prinsjesdag budget documents to police, while admitting such probes rarely succeed.
body: At his weekly press conference on 4 September, Prime Minister Rob Jetten said the government will file a criminal complaint over the leaking of confidential budget papers to the media, calling it a matter of principle. He conceded such investigations often lead nowhere.

He also wants clearer agreements with the Tweede Kamer on handling embargoed documents so everyone receives them at the same time. RTL Nieuws reported leaked 2027 budget details this week, ahead of Finance Minister Eelco Heinen's Prinsjesdag presentation on Tuesday 15 September.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet drops welfare cuts and delays asset tax reform to 2029
netherlands.summary: Leaked plans show the coalition dropped most of its 6.5 billion euro welfare cuts and will spend 1.5 billion euros on purchasing power, while box 3 reform slips to 2029.
body: The Jetten cabinet has scrapped most planned cuts to unemployment and incapacity benefits to win opposition support for the 2027 budget, RTL Nieuws reported, and will delay a health excess rise while spending 1.5 billion euros offsetting inflation. This is a setback for the VVD, which resisted compromise.

The coalition is ten seats short in the lower house and 16 short in the Senate, and opposition talks ended without a deal. DutchNews.nl reports box 3 tax reform is likely delayed to 2029, as the interim refund system costs about 2 billion euros a year.

netherlands.h3: Port workers down tools as national transport strike looms Wednesday
netherlands.summary: Dockers in Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Zeeland stopped work on 4 September against social security cuts, ahead of a 24-hour national transport strike on 9 September.
body: FNV Havens and CNV struck on 4 September at the ports of Rotterdam, Amsterdam, Vlissingen and Terneuzen, halting ship handling in parts of Rotterdam from 11:15 to 19:00 and delaying road, rail and inland shipping. Operator ECT expects the backlog to take days to clear.

Unions demand the cabinet withdraw its 6.5 billion euro social security cut, including halving unemployment benefit duration and trimming the WIA scheme. The action precedes a national transport strike on Wednesday 9 September, when NS will run no trains except the Airport Sprinter.

netherlands.h3: Russian embassy in The Hague uses ON! podcaster as propaganda amplifier
netherlands.summary: Justice for Prosperity said on 4 September that 40 percent of the Russian embassy's posts follow propaganda patterns, amplified over 50 times by podcaster Jan Bennink.
body: Justice for Prosperity analysed over 200 posts by the Russian embassy in The Hague over ten months and concluded on 4 September the account mainly acts as a propaganda channel, with about 45 percent targeting Dutch affairs. Its verified name lets the embassy evade EU sanctions applied to outlets like RT.

The platform named ON! podcaster Jan Bennink, whose two X accounts have over 70,000 followers, as reposting embassy content over 50 times. The broadcaster risks losing its status after former editor Joost Niemoller praised aspects of Hitler and resigned.

netherlands.h3: PBL backs nitrogen plan but says livestock herd must shrink
netherlands.summary: The Environmental Assessment Agency said on 3 September the cabinet's nitrogen plan is a major step forward, but requires a substantial cut in livestock numbers.
body: The Planbureau voor de Leefomgeving assessed the cabinet's nitrogen plans on 3 September as a serious step forward after years of stalemate, giving the package a comfortable pass. The report says the measures will still require a significant shrinking of the national herd.

Buy-out schemes and stricter rules will push farmers to cut cattle, pig and poultry numbers, as the plan still falls short of legal targets in some areas, DutchNews.nl reports. The findings will feed into the budget debate, where farm groups and the BBB are expected to push back.

netherlands.h3: Rents rise 4.4 percent, smallest increase in three years
netherlands.summary: CBS said on 4 September that rents rose 4.4 percent in July, the smallest increase in three years, down from 4.9 percent in 2025, with Rotterdam seeing the steepest rise.
body: Rents in the Netherlands rose 4.4 percent in July from a year earlier, CBS reported on 4 September, down from 4.9 percent in 2025 and 5.4 percent in 2024. Private tenants saw the largest hikes at 4.5 percent, against 3.8 percent for sitting tenants, while corporations raised social rents 4.4 percent.

Among the big four cities, Rotterdam recorded the highest rise at 4.7 percent, while Amsterdam, Utrecht and The Hague ranged from 4.3 to 4.5 percent. The figures come as the student room shortage remains above 20,000 despite new construction.

netherlands.h3: Direct Norway to Netherlands gas pipeline moves to next phase
netherlands.summary: North Sea operator Nogat said on 4 September it is advancing a direct Norway to Netherlands gas pipeline, targeting 2029 and 15 percent of Dutch demand.
body: Nogat announced on 4 September it is moving to the next stage of a direct gas link between Norway and the Netherlands after a positive feasibility study. A direct link, bypassing current routes via the UK, Germany and Belgium, would add over 4 billion cubic metres a year, about 15 percent of demand, from 2029.

Director Falco van Wissen said a third of European gas imports already come from the Norwegian North Sea and pipeline gas cuts dependence on the US or Middle East. Shareholders including EBN and PGGM will decide on investment in mid-2027.

netherlands.h3: Road traffic CO2 falls for first time since the pandemic
netherlands.summary: CBS figures published on 4 September show Dutch road traffic emitted 26.6 billion kg of CO2 in 2025, down from just over 27 billion, the first fall since the pandemic.
body: Road traffic in the Netherlands emitted 26.6 billion kilograms of CO2 in 2025, against a little over 27 billion the year before, CBS reported on 4 September, the first decline since the pandemic. Passenger cars account for more than half the total at 15 billion kilograms.

CBS attributes the drop mainly to growing numbers of fully electric cars, which emit nothing while driving, though the figures exclude emissions from generating that electricity. Scooters showed the largest relative increase but make up only 0.2 percent of emissions.

netherlands.h3: DNB moved a quarter of its gold out of the US citing geopolitical unrest
netherlands.summary: De Nederlandsche Bank confirmed this week it moved over a quarter of its gold reserves from the US and Canada to the Bank of England between March and August.
body: De Nederlandsche Bank said on 2 September it moved over a quarter of the Dutch gold reserves, worth around 10 billion euros, from the United States and Canada to London between March and August, citing geopolitical unrest. The New York Times reports the Bank of England's vaults hold the world's most tradable bullion.

The move follows similar reviews by other European central banks since the Iran war began. DNB says the decision is about diversification and liquidity, though the timing has been widely read as a sign of eroding confidence in Washington.

netherlands.h3: Officials among thousands posting homophobic abuse at Jetten, AD finds
netherlands.summary: An AD analysis on 4 September found 2,293 homophobic replies to Jetten's 323 posts on X since February, including from council, police and air force staff.
body: Algemeen Dagblad analysed 45,860 replies to Jetten's 323 posts on the PM's X account since February and found 2,293, one in twenty, were homophobic, the paper reported on 4 September. Abuse appeared under almost every post, mostly from ordinary users rather than organised trolls.

AD identified repeat accounts including a government social support official, a police employee and an air force member. Jetten files weekly police reports without stemming the flow, as the Netherlands slips to 13th of 49 on ILGA-Europe's Rainbow Index.

netherlands.h3: Dutch soil scientist wins Ig Nobel for burying 1,000 pairs of underpants
netherlands.summary: Dutch soil scientist Marcel van der Heijden shared the 2026 Ig Nobel prize for soil science on 3 September for burying 1,000 pairs of underpants in 25 countries.
body: Marcel van der Heijden of the University of Zurich and three colleagues won the Ig Nobel prize for soil science at the 36th ceremony in Zurich on 3 September. Volunteers in more than 25 countries buried identical cotton underpants and dug them up two months later, with more rotted fabric meaning healthier soil.

Van der Heijden said the results show soil management significantly affects fertility and ecosystems. It was the first ceremony held outside the US in three decades, and Dutch researchers have won 22 Ig Nobels since 1991.

netherlands.h3: National water shortage officially over, but Rhine still at half flow
netherlands.summary: The infrastructure ministry downgraded the country from an actual to an impending water shortage on 3 September, though the Rhine may stay at half flow until year end.
body: The Netherlands moved from level two to level one on its three-stage water shortage scale on 3 September, the infrastructure ministry said, as rain, cooler weather and less irrigation eased demand. The crisis team that met weekly through summer will disband.

The Rhine still carries only about half its normal volume for early September, and stranded houseboats will not refloat until levels rise. Restrictions remain in the east and south, and IJsselmeer salinisation still concerns drinking water firms, though supplies remain secure.

netherlands.h3: Warm weekend ahead as NS bans bags on seats
netherlands.summary: After a code yellow for coastal winds on Friday, Saturday brings 20 to 22 degrees with up to 30 possible on Monday, as NS bans bags on seats from 4 September.
body: The KNMI issued a code yellow on 4 September for gusts of 75 to 90 kilometres per hour along the coast, with Saturday calmer at 20 to 22 degrees under sun and cloud. Sunday and Monday turn summery warm at 27 to 28 degrees, possibly 30 in the south, before wind and rain return Tuesday.

A formal NS ban on placing bags on seats took effect on 4 September, though passengers will only be asked to move bags, not removed from trains. NS also said it will stop compensating travellers for cancellations caused by strikes.
